Unofficial until approved by the
  Alhambra City Council
  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  March 11, 2024
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:21 p.m., on Monday, March 11, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Police Chief Kennedy, Fire Chief
Ragusa

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIALS

1.  PROCLAMATIONS – F2M24-3

  A.  The Alhambra City Council ratified the action of Mayor Maza in proclaiming the month
  of March, 2024 as WOMEN’S HISTORY MONTH in Alhambra.

  B.  The Alhambra City Council ratified the action of Mayor Maza in proclaiming March,
  2024 as RED CROSS MONTH in Alhambra. Mayor MAZA presented the Red Cross
  Month proclamation to Diana Pineda RAMIREZ, Executive Director of the San Gabriel
  and Pomona Valley Chapter of the American Red Cross.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St. spoke regarding Women’s
  History Month and the background of the Women’s Suffrage Movement in the United States.

PRESENTATION

2.  ADOPTION OF THE BICYCLE AND PEDESTRIAN IMPROVEMENT PLAN;
  AUTHORIZATION TO REALLOCATE MEASURE R FUNDS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION
  OF BICYCLE AND PEDESTRIAN PLAN PROJECTS; AND ACCEPTANCE OF
  ENVIRONMENTAL EXEMPTION DETERMINATION – F2M22-33, M2M24-47

3-11-24  1
   Assistant City Manager GARCIA delivered a staff report and Ryan Johnson, from Alta Planning
  + Design, delivered a presentation which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. On January 8,
  2024, staff presented the Bike and Pedestrian Improvement Plan for the Council’s
  consideration, pursuant to data collection, a needs assessment, and public engagement
  conducted throughout the Plan process. This Plan was a directive under the City’s Strategic
  Plan under the goals of Enhancing Public Safety, Improving Infrastructure and Mobility, and
  Promoting Sustainability. The Plan presented on January 8, 2024 was not adopted by the
  Council; rather, based on public comment for additional time to review the document,
  consideration to adopt the Plan was tabled to the February 12th meeting. Staff and the City’s
  consultant conducted a virtual workshop on January 23, 2024; a Special Meeting with the
  Transportation Commission on January 24, 2024; and an in-person workshop at the Library
  on February 1, 2024. On January 24, 2024, the Transportation Commission submitted a
  recommendation to adopt the Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvement Plan, contingent on also
  aligning the Plan with Metro’s recent update to their Active Transportation Plan (for regional
  connectivity benefits) and removing the McLean Bridge from the City’s pedestrian or bicycle
  network. On February 12, 2024, the Plan was resubmitted for the City Council’s consideration.
  Based on input received that the Asian Pacific Islander Forward Movement (APIFM), a non-
  profit organization, wished to provide feedback regarding the Plan, the Council directed the
  adoption of the Plan be rescheduled to March to allow time for the City’s consultant to collect
  this information or any other public comments received for further analysis. Feedback provided
  by APIFM included approximately 200 written comments, with many responses focused on
  improvements near Fremont Elementary School, such as installing high-visibility crosswalks,
  compliance with speed limits and ambitious traffic calming infrastructure. Alhambra’s Bicycle
  and Pedestrian Improvement Plan highlighted a Backbone Bicycle Network, Full Network
  (comprehensive), and Further Study Network, with a description of the facility types or bicycle
  lane classification. In addition, it included “priority” pedestrian improvements zones based on
  demand, major destinations and barriers, and safety. The estimated costs for Alhambra’s
  bicycle infrastructure were between $8 million and $32 million, for up to 50 miles of bike
  network, not including costs subject to further study. The estimated costs for the pedestrian
  improvements at eight priority areas of the City were approximately $15 million.

  The Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvement Plan is available for public review via the City’s
  website at https://www.cityofalhambra.org/228/Notices-Documents.

  Public Comment:

  The following people spoke in favor of the Plan:
  1) Elliot Lee, 812 Cutis Ln., also made additional suggestions regarding traffic calming measures.
  2) Victor Dorado, 901 Novelda Rd.
  3) Je-Show Yang also made additional suggestions regarding bike lanes and traffic calming
  measures.
  4) Andrew Lau, 712 W. Ramona Rd.
  5) Omar Galicia, 101 E. Beacon St., also submitted his comments via email, and made additional
  suggestions.
  6) Shirley Tatsuno, 1408 S. Fifth St.
  7) Xana Hermosillo, 225 Palmetto Dr.
  8) Henry Aviles, via Zoom, also made additional suggestions regarding parking and bike lanes.
  9) Jean Park, via Zoom
  10) Esther Tam, via Zoom
  11) Michael Lawrence, via Zoom

  The following people provided additional suggestions:
  1) Jennifer Ng, S. Cordova St.
  2) Lewis McCammon, 105 N. Cordova St.

  2
3-11-24
   Public comment received via email and on file in the City Clerk’s office:
  The following people wrote in favor of the Plan:
  1)  Jennifer Van
  2)  Jenna Cobb
  3)  Brenda Chi
  4)  Anna Van

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. JOHNSON discussed parking
  concerns at Alhambra Park given the high attendance of visitors for the variety of programming
  available. Mr. JOHNSON reiterated that this was a high-level planning document and none of
  the recommendations were set in stone as far as concept. He stated that until the studies were
  completed with regards to parking capacity, parking use, ADA access, and traffic, that the
  suggestions were not set in stone and they were continuing to explore other options. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER continued to discuss the area around Alhambra Park with Director of
  Public Works RAY and other options for parking. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER discussed the
  installation of pedestrian countdown signals in other areas of the city, such as Chapel Ave.
  and Main St. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER motioned to approve the Plan.

  Councilmember LEE and Mr. JOHNSON discussed the process of creating the Plan, the
  adoption of the Plan, grant opportunities for funding programs related to the Plan, and the
  implementation of projects depending on grant funds received. Ms. LEE stated that she fully
  supported the pedestrian portion of the Plan. Ms. LEE and Mr. JOHNSON further discussed
  the promotional phase of the Plan to demonstrate or test various projects, how council would
  determine which projects to demonstrate, the need for further studies on certain areas, and
  grant funds for corridor specific planning. Ms. LEE went on to discuss the traffic impact for
  certain corridors and specifically the Main St. corridor. Mr. JOHNSON continued to respond to
  questions. Ms. LEE discussed her concerns with emergency vehicle access to Main St. due
  to the proposed high comfort bike lanes. Mr. JOHNSON and Vice Mayor PÉREZ responded
  to her. Ms. LEE expressed concern with the public responses received thus far for the project
  and that many affected by the proposed plan would not provide adequate input. She further
  expressed concern with the proposed changes for Almansor Park and the lack of parking
  spaces. Ms. LEE also expressed concern with available parking in areas with rental high-
  density units or other residential areas. Ms. LEE discussed the element of equity in the studies
  used for the Plan with Mr. JOHNSON. Ms. LEE and Mr. JOHNSON continued to discuss the
  number of parking spaces which may be eliminated, the redesign of parking capacity, and the
  need for parking studies. Ms. LEE went on to discuss the possibility of bikers to ride on the
  sidewalk which she argued would offer better protection and would not result in parking
  reduction. She continued to discuss the negative impact of parking reduction on businesses.
  She emphasized that she supported the Plan as long as each project could be reviewed
  individually by Council and additional studies would be conducted for each project.

  Councilmember MALONEY and Ms. LEE discussed the conceptual nature of the Plan versus
  the impact of each proposed project. Ms. LEE continued to express concerns and echoed
  previous discussion regarding the next steps for implementing various projects. Mr. JOHNSON
  responded to questions. Ms. LEE made a substitute motion to remove all high comfort level
  bicycle lanes from the Plan until they could be further studied. After receiving no second, the
  motion failed.

  Mr. MALONEY seconded the first motion made by Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER for approval.

  Mr. MALONEY reiterated that this was a high-level conceptual document and that there would
  be many opportunities for greater input. He spoke to the importance of the Bicycle and
  Pedestrian Improvement Plan and expressed appreciation for all parties who contributed in
  the development of the Plan. He continued to speak regarding the importance of bicycle and
  pedestrian safety, the ability of the plan to address safety measures, and requested an
  3
3-11-24
   agendized discussion regarding the implementation of a program which would allow for speed
  calming devices to be added in residential neighborhoods. Vice Mayor PÉREZ supported an
  agendized discussion. Ms. PÉREZ, Mr. MALONEY, and Mr. JOHNSON discussed the use of
  speed tables in the plan. Council agreed to an agendized discussion.

  Vice Mayor PÉREZ, Mr. JOHNSON, and Director of Public Works RAY discussed Citywide
  daylighting elements in crosswalks and corners, leading intervals in crosswalks and
  intersections, and the status of traffic studies near the intersection of Cordova and Main
  Streets. Ms. PÉREZ went on to discuss the ways that the active transportation movement
  would necessitate changes to the City, the outcry from the community for active transportation
  programs, the changes necessary to ensure pedestrian and bike safety, elements of equity in
  transportation elements, and the continued need for community outreach. She supported Ms.
  Andrade-Stadler’s motion to approve the Plan.

  Mayor MAZA thanked the public, staff, Alta Planning + Design, and the Council Subcommittee
  for their work on the Plan. He supported the Plan, acknowledged Ms. Lee’s concerns as well
  as some concerns from the public, and reiterated that the City would continue to receive public
  input and address concerns. He supported approval of the Plan.

  City Attorney MONTES and Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER clarified the motion.

  After the vote, Ms. LEE responded to comments made by Ms. PÉREZ, stating that she
  disagreed with her logic and clarified an anecdote regarding a pedestrian incident at Alhambra
  Park.

  Action Taken: City Council took the following actions:

  A.  Accepted the Council Subcommittee’s request to adopt the Bicycle and Pedestrian
  Improvement Plan (Plan);
  B.  Directed staff to move forward with the Backbone Bicycle Network and the Priority
  Pedestrian Improvements, contingent on obtaining all the necessary funding;
  C.  Authorized staff to request a reallocation of $14.4 million in Measure R Funds from the
  Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) toward the
  implementation of Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvement Plan projects;
  D.  Accepted the environmental review exemption determination for this Plan; and,
  E.  Directed staff undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-
  47)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded: MALONEY
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Abstain:  LEE
  Absent:  NONE

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 3 – 18)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda were considered by the City Council to be routine were
enacted by one motion.

3.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON MARENGO
  AVENUE – F2M24-34, N2M24-37

  The 10-inch cast iron water main on Marengo Avenue between Grand Avenue and Alhambra
  Road was installed in 1966. This segment of water main has had a history of breaks, causing

  4
3-11-24
   interruption of water service and damage to the road. Replacing the water main would greatly
  improve flow, firefighting capabilities, and overall system reliability. Plans and specifications
  were prepared. Staff reviewed the plans and found them to be consistent with the City’s
  standards.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Water Main Replacement Project on Marengo Avenue with bids
  due no later than 10:30 a.m. on April 4, 2024, and opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

4.  RATIFICATION OF CONTRACT NO. C2M24-14 FOR THE 2024 EMERGENCY ROOF
  REPAIR PROJECT – F2M24-36, C2M24-14, M2M24-39

  The recent rain storms caused significant damage to City owned buildings. The Utilities
  Warehouse and offices at the City Yard, Fire Station 71, the Communications Building, Fire
  Station 74, and the flat roof areas of Fire Station 72 experienced significant damage caused
  by roof leakage during the recent storms. These buildings house personnel, equipment and
  materials critical to providing the essential services to Alhambra. City staff did not have the
  proper equipment or specialized skills to make the required repairs. As such, staff contacted
  the contractor that recently provided the lowest bid and installed a new roof at the Police
  Department building. Wiltshire Urethane Foam Company could perform the work in a timely
  manner to prevent further intrusion, damage and harm to City facilities and personnel.
  Emergency contract for this work was permissible under Alhambra Municipal Code Chapter
  3.36.070(A)(4).

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council ratified Contract No. C2M24-14 with Wiltshire Urethane
  Foam Company for the 2024 Emergency Roof Repair Project in the amount of $367,992.00;
  and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-39)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  AWARD CONTRACT: INSTALLATION OF PEDESTRIAN COUNTDOWN SIGNAL HEAD
  SYSTEMS PROJECT AT VARIOUS INTERSECTIONS THROUGHOUT THE CITY (HSIP-
  5130(022)) – F2M23-73, N2M23-137, C2M24-16, M2M24-40

  The Installation of Pedestrian Countdown Signal Head Systems Project (HSIP-5130(022))
  consists of installing countdown signal heads at various intersections throughout the City. The
  City Council authorized a Notice Inviting Bids for the Project on November 13. 2023. On
  January 4, 2024, the City Clerk received two bids that ranged from $170,920.00 to
  $212,928.00. Staff reviewed the bids and found the one received from Bear Electrical
  Solutions, Inc. in the amount of $170,920.00 to be the lowest responsible bid. Bear Electrical

  5
3-11-24
   Solutions, Inc. had the necessary licenses to complete the work and had conducted similar
  projects for the City of Alhambra.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Bear Electrical Solutions, Inc. in the amount of
  $170,920.00 for the Installation of Pedestrian Countdown Signal Head Systems Project at
  various intersections throughout the City (HSIP-5130(022)); and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-40)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: HEATING, VENTILATION AND AIR CONDITIONING (HVAC)
  MAINTENANCE FOR CITY HALL, CIVIC CENTER LIBRARY, POLICE DEPARTMENT AND
  FIRE STATION NO. 71 – F2M22-44, C2M22-42, M2M24-41

  The City entered into a three-year contract with Allison Mechanical, Inc. for Heating,
  Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) maintenance services, commencing on August 1,
  2022 until June 30, 2025. To improve service and provide better maintenance of the HVAC
  systems of the Fire Department’s facilities not currently included in the contract, staff requested
  quotes from Allison Mechanical for Fire Stations 72, 73, and 74 and the Training Facility.
  Services for these locations are currently completed on an as-needed or on-call basis. Staff
  sought to include these facilities on a quarterly preventive maintenance schedule. Allison
  Mechanical submitted a proposal for an additional $14,457.00 for the remaining two years of
  the contract.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and
  Allison Mechanical, Inc. for Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) maintenance
  services for an additional $14,457 for a contract amount not to exceed $349,653; and, directed
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-41)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  APPROVAL OF MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT FOR THE 626 GOLDEN STREETS
  MISSION TO MISSION 2024 EVENT – F2M23-16, C2M24-17, M2M24-42

  On July 24, 2024, the City Council approved the intent to participate in the 626 Golden Streets
  Mission to Mission event and authorized the City Manager or Designee to execute the
  Memorandum of Understanding. The SGVCOG was successful in securing $400,000 in
  Proposition C funds to host the 626 Golden Streets Mission-to-Mission, including outreach,
  pre-event planning, and day of event staging costs. The Event programming required a set
  amount of in-kind or local fund match. The SGVCOG and the cities partnered together to host
  the Event as a contiguous open street event on Sunday, April 28, 2024, from South Pasadena
  6
3-11-24
   to San Gabriel. The City of Alhambra would provide a $22,500 in-kind match and would be
  eligible for up to $10,000 in program funding. Each agency would host activities in their hub.
  Alhambra’s hub would be in downtown Alhambra in conjunction with the Farmers Market and
  Eco Fair.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a Memorandum of Agreement, subject to final
  language approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the San Gabriel
  Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG) and the cities of Alhambra, San Gabriel, and South
  Pasadena to share resources and host the 626 Golden Streets Mission to Mission event, on
  April 28, 2024; authorize the City Manager to execute said MOA; and, direct staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-42)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  APPROVE CONTRACT CHANGE ORDER: ELECTRICAL UPGRADING ON WELL NO. 9
  PROJECT – F2M22-36, C2M23-16, M2M24-43

  On March 27, 2023, the City Council awarded a contract to Faith Electric LLC for the Electrical
  Upgrading on Well No. 9 Project in an amount not to exceed $359,552.00. In order to complete
  the planned replacement of the motor control center Southern California Edison required the
  City to underground the existing electrical service to Well No. 9. Change Order No. 1 included
  not only undergrounding the SCE electrical service, but also the demolishing an existing SCE
  pad and enclosure, removing and replacing the existing conduit to the new motor control center
  panels, and installing new concrete pads with protective bollards.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved Change Order No. 1 for the Electrical Upgrading
  on Well No. 9 Project, increasing Contract No. C2M23-16 with Faith Electric LLC by
  $117,284.45.00, bringing the total revised contract value to an amount not to exceed
  $476,836.45; directed the Finance Director to appropriate funds from the Water Fund Balance
  and allocate to account number 401.80.8884.92135; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-43)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  RESOLUTION UPDATING VEHICLE MILES TRAVELED (VMT) THRESHOLDS OF
  SIGNIFICANCE FOR PURPOSES OF ANALYZING TRANSPORTATION IMPACTS UNDER
  THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA) – F2M20-44, R2M24-7

  On June 8, 2020, with guidance from the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments
  (SGVCOG), the City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M20-22 adopting VMT thresholds of
  significance for purposes of analyzing transportation impacts under the CEQA, before the new
  CEQA Guidelines section 15064.3 went into effect on July 1, 2020. The SGVCOG produced
  the current tool for assessing VMT. The tool is based on VMT outputs from the Southern
  California Association of Government’s (SCAG) 2016 Regional Transportation
  Plan/Sustainable Communities Strategy (RTP/SCS) which was trip-based. The model needed
  to be updated to the 2020 RTP/SCS model, which is activity-based. The change of both the
  type of model (trip-based model versus activity-based) and the underlying data, such as traffic
  counts and socioeconomic data, resulted in changes to the VMT threshold numbers and low
  VMT areas.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-7 entitled: A Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of Alhambra updating the “Vehicle Miles Traveled” Thresholds
  of Significance for purposes of analyzing transportation impacts under the California
  Environmental Quality Act; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action.
  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

11,  EXTENSION OF AGREEMENT FOR SERVICES WITH THE REGENTS OF THE
  UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA – F2M5-77, C2M19-40, M2M24-45

  8
3-11-24
   On April 1, 2016, the City contracted with the Regents of the University of California on behalf
  of the UCLA Center for Prehospital Care to provide continuing education programs and Quality
  Improvement services. The term of the agreement was extended through March 31, 2024.
  Due to the contract expiring on March 31, 2024 and the fact that the contractor continued to
  perform satisfactory service, staff reached out to The Regents of the University of California to
  obtain rates for a five-year term, if authorized. The total cost for the 5-year term would be
  $134,604.38. Increase costs were the result of inflation and wage increases.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a second amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to the agreement with The Regents of the
  University of California for continuing education programs and Quality Improvement services
  for five years through March 31, 2029 at a cost not to exceed $134,604.38; authorized the
  Chief of Police to execute said amendment; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-45)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

12.  APPROVAL OF A WEBSITE SERVICES CONTRACT WITH CIVICPLUS, LLC – F2M24-35,
  C2M24-15, M2M24-46

  CivicPlus, LLC (CivicPlus) provides website hosting and security services for the City of
  Alhambra. CivicPlus’s website hosting and security has been critical to all department
  operations as well as residents and community members. The City’s website has hosted news
  and announcements, Requests for Proposals and Bid notices, meeting agendas, facilitates
  community engagement, and more. The City sought to retain the website hosting and security
  services with CivicPlus. Staff requested the City Council approve a contract with CivicPlus for
  five years, with the option to extend one two-year term, for continued support to the City’s
  website. Working with them since 2021, services have been satisfactory, and the City sought
  to continue use of the CivicPlus platform, which is proprietary. Sole source purchase is
  allowable per Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080, section (B)(2), which states: “The supply or
  equipment can only be obtained by one source (“sole source”).

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract with CivicPlus, LLC for hosting the
  City’s website and related security services in the amount of $102,335.38 over five years
  through April 29, 2029, with the option to extend for one additional two-year term, subject to
  final language approval and review by the City Attorney and the City Manager; authorized the
  City Manager to exercise the option to extend, subject to satisfactory performance and Council
  budget appropriation. (M2M24-46)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, PÉREZ, MALONEY, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

  9
3-11-24
 13.  APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS AND AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR THE LEASE AND
  SERVICES OF DRONE AS FIRST RESPONDER SYSTEM AND EQUIPMENT – F2M24-6B,
  C2M24-18, M2M24-48

  The Police Department sought to upgrade its existing Unmanned Aerial Support (UAS)
  capabilities with Aerodome. Aerodome provides an all-in-one platform including drone
  hardware, software, radar, regulatory services and ongoing support for Drone as First
  Responder (DFR) operations. This platform delivers critical situational awareness for officers
  responding to emergency situations and aids Police response times. Due to the unique nature
